messages:
alex: Heads-up — nightly perf CI flagged a p95 surge on the small-batch benchmark at ~02:12 UTC. Run 2026-03-16_02. Skimming logs now, but wanted to ping the runtime team before digging deeper. cc @chen @maria
ci-bot: Test run 2026-03-16_02 completed. 48 tests, 12 breaching p95 threshold. Dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/perf/runs/2026-03-16_02 (summary attached).
chen: Thanks. Do we have the failing test names + commit hash for that run? Any repro steps? Could be scheduler tweak from last week.
alex: Commit: a1b2c3d -> c3d4e5f (rolled 03/15). Quick numbers from the summary:
```
p50 baseline: 110ms -> 115ms (stable)
p95 baseline: 210ms -> 640ms (+430ms)
gpu_util: 78% -> 32% (spikes of kernel_wakeup)
kernel_wait_ms: +350ms
```
logs: https://console.redwood.ai/logs/2026-03-16_02/small-batch/ (grep for "kernel_wakeup")
maria: If p50 is stable and p95 jumps, likely a tail-scheduling/packing issue. I can start a bisect on infra. Want me to run binary search between a1b2c3d and c3d4e5f?
niko: Started bisect job #bisect-672 against bench infra (br-4187). ETA ~25m. Also enabled sampling profiler for the run: https://console.redwood.ai/profiler/bisect-672
chen: Reproducer command? I'd like to run locally with --batcher=continuous and the same seq distribution.
alex: Repro command we use in CI: `pytest tests/bench/test_small_batch.py::test_tail_latency --runslow --bench=small_batch --seed=42` with env `REDWOOD_BATCHER=continuous REDWOOD_MAX_SEQ=512`. Also note we disable prefix cache in CI for small-batch suite.
niko: Bisect update: midpoint commit d2d3d4e shows partial regression (p95 +180ms). Narrowing. The profiler is showing increased context-switch waits around the scheduler handoff; attaching flame: https://console.redwood.ai/profiler/bisect-672/flame.svg
maria: If bisect hits the change that added `prefer_late_batch` switch in scheduler, that's our suspect. If confirmed we should add a runtime flag gate and revert the default until we tweak packing heuristics. I'll draft a small fallback PR (tag: perf-hotfix) and can ship to dedicated canary.
ench: (typo) chen: +1 on fallback PR. Also double-check kernel versions on bench infra — I saw one node on 525.10 that had different NUMA latency last week.
alex: Good catch. I’ll coordinate infra to verify kernel versions and node config for the failing run. For now plan: 1) wait for bisect result (~20m), 2) if bisect identifies commit, open perf-hotfix PR to gate feature, 3) run canary on dedicated capacity, 4) notify support if customer-facing SLOs impacted.
ci-bot: bisect-672 completed: culprit commit identified -> c3d4e5f (scheduler: prefer_late_batch). Regression reproduced locally at `HEAD~2`.
maria: On it — creating PR with opt-in flag and fallback to previous packing algo. Will request urgent review from @alex and @chen.
niko: Quick note: if anyone wants to reproduce faster, run `./tools/run_bench --profile --seed 42 --cases small_batch --concurrency 8`. Helps trigger tail behavior quicker.
chen: Thanks all. If the PR looks good I can approve and we can roll the fallback to canary this afternoon. Keep this thread updated, tagging ops if we flip any infra flags. :thumbsup:
